findings.title: contractor-matching-ai treats missing cert/license valid_until as date.max → expired prequal bypass
findings.description: _filter_eligible builds eligible cert/license sets with `c.get('valid_until', date.max) >= date.today()` (same for licenses). Attacker-controlled ContractorProfile certifications/licenses that omit `valid_until` (or supply only name/type) are treated as never-expiring. Control profiles with the same certs dated in the past are correctly rejected. No insurance_coverage hard gate; safety scores trust self-reported fatality_count/incident_rate. Forged profiles then rank in find_matches / BidEvaluator recommendations.
findings.impact: Unlicensed / expired-cert contractors pass prequalification and surface as top matches / Strongly Recommended bids → award to unqualified parties and safety/compliance exposure.
attack_path: Register ContractorProfile with required cert names and license types but omit valid_until keys; set operating_regions, specializations, workload <95, self-reported fatality_count=0.
Submit ProjectRequirements requiring those certs/licenses.
_filter_eligible includes attacker (date.max); control with valid_until=2020-01-01 is excluded.
find_matches / evaluate_bids returns attacker with competitive total_score for award recommendation.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not open-estimate underbid. Not previously filed contractor findings. Distinct privilege/prequal fail-open on the eligibility gate itself via date.max default.
key_snippets: contractor_certs = set(c['name'] for c in contractor.certifications if c.get('valid_until', date.max) >= date.today())
contractor_licenses = set(l['type'] for l in contractor.licenses if l.get('valid_until', date.max) >= date.today())
PoC: Shadow Prefab LLC eligible score=64; Honest Co with dated-expired certs excluded

findings.title: enterprise-risk-aggregator trusts caller probability with no clamp → CRITICAL risks score LOW / VaR=0
findings.description: add_risk / import_project_risks accept attacker-chosen probability with no validation (allowed 0, negative, >1). score=probability*impact and level thresholds use that product only. A $10M structural-collapse risk at p=0.8 is CRITICAL (score $8M); the same impact at p=0 is LOW with score=0. generate_portfolio_profile expected_loss and Monte Carlo VaR95 then collapse to $0, hiding systemic portfolio exposure.
findings.impact: Malicious or negligent project risk registers erase enterprise CRITICAL safety/financial risks from portfolio reports, VaR, and mitigation priorities → false risk appetite and unfunded contingencies.
attack_path: Call import_project_risks with category=safety, impact=10000000, probability=0.0 (or 0.01).
generate_portfolio_profile() → level=LOW, expected_loss=0, var_95=0.
Contrast control p=0.8 → CRITICAL, expected_loss=8000000, VaR≈10000000.
Portfolio dashboard / mitigation priorities omit the risk.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not cwicr risk min/max. Not weather gates. Prompt-targeted fail-open risk scoring with end-to-end portfolio VaR impact; no prior finding ID on this skill.
key_snippets: self.score = self.probability * self.impact
probability=r['probability']  # import_project_risks, unvalidated
if random.random() < risk.probability: sim_loss += risk.impact
PoC: p=0 → LOW score=0 expected_loss=0 VaR95=0 vs p=0.8 CRITICAL

findings.title: sensor-data-aggregator DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS omit STRAIN/TILT/PRESSURE → catastrophic readings never alert
findings.description: SensorType includes PRESSURE/STRAIN/TILT (structural integrity) but DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS only covers temperature/humidity/vibration/noise/AQI/dust/gas. register_sensor(thresholds=None) sets thresholds={}. ingest_reading marks quality GOOD (no min/max) and _check_thresholds never fires without warning/critical keys. 45° tilt or extreme strain produce zero alerts while GAS control at 80ppm correctly alerts CRITICAL. Separately, any authenticated-or-not ingest of spoofed-safe gas values suppresses alerts (IoT spoof accept).
findings.impact: Structural / tilt / pressure monitoring deployed as written is alert-blind → missed collapse/settlement indicators; spoofed-safe gas readings silence confined-space CRITICAL alarms.
attack_path: Register TILT/STRAIN sensors with default thresholds (as skill Quick Start / register_sensor).
ingest_reading(TILT, 45.0) and ingest_reading(STRAIN, 5000) → alerts=[].
Optional: ingest_reading(GAS, 5) while real atmosphere is hazardous → no CRITICAL.
Dashboard get_zone_summary / generate_report show healthy with no alerts.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior discard was SUSPECT quality still storing out-of-range env readings. This is missing default gates for structural SensorTypes so CRITICAL never exists — same class as weather unused max_wind, different skill/sink.
key_snippets: STRAIN = "strain"; TILT = "tilt"; PRESSURE = "pressure"
DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS = { TEMPERATURE, HUMIDITY, VIBRATION, NOISE, AIR_QUALITY, DUST, GAS }  # no structural
thresholds = self.DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS.get(sensor_type, {})
PoC: tilt=45 / strain=5000 → 0 alerts; gas=80 → CRITICAL

findings.title: change-order-analysis allows negative CostBreakdown totals and approve() from DRAFT → undercounted impact + forged approval
findings.description: CostBreakdown.total sums labor/materials/equipment/subcontractor/overhead/profit with no non-negativity checks. Attacker sets large positive direct costs offset by negative profit/overhead so total collapses (e.g. $2M components → $50k). _calculate_severity then classifies MINOR. approve() has no status gate — DRAFT COs become APPROVED with arbitrary approver string. get_summary total_cost_impact / cost_impact_pct report the undercounted figure.
findings.impact: Owner exposure and schedule/cost risk from change orders are understated in analysis reports; forged APPROVED status legitimizes undercounted COs in downstream workflows.
attack_path: create_change_order(...) → DRAFT.
update_cost(CostBreakdown(labor=1.5e6, materials=5e5, profit=-1.9e6, overhead=-5e4)) → total=50000, severity=MINOR.
approve(co_id, 'forged-approver') without submit_for_approval → APPROVED.
get_summary() reports total_cost_impact=50000 (0.5% of $10M contract) instead of ~$2M.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Sibling DRAFT-approve exists on curated change-order-manager, but this finding's primary chain is negative-component undercount into severity+summary (prompt: change-order undercount). Filed as one combined HIGH on the innovative analysis skill.
key_snippets: return self.labor + self.materials + self.equipment + self.subcontractor + self.overhead + self.profit
def approve(...): if co: ... co.status = ChangeOrderStatus.APPROVED  # no DRAFT/SUBMITTED check
total_cost = sum(co.cost_breakdown.total for co in self.change_orders.values())
PoC: $2M components → total=50000 MINOR + DRAFT→APPROVED

findings.title: digital-twin-sync import_from_ifc silently replaces elements → wipes COMPLETED status; unauth WS/MQTT write path
findings.description: import_from_ifc always does `self.elements[element.element_id] = element` with a fresh DigitalTwinElement defaulting to PLANNED — no merge of status/properties/history. Re-importing an attacker-crafted IFC (or replaying import) for an in-progress/completed element wipes field progress to PLANNED. TwinSynchronizer WebSocket accepts unauthenticated `update` / `status_update` messages that call update_property / update_status; MQTT sensors/# has no auth and process_sensor_update overwrites bound properties.
findings.impact: As-built / progress twin state can be reset or forged (COMPLETED wiped or falsely set), corrupting progress billing, schedule integration, and live monitoring.
attack_path: Field marks WALL-001 COMPLETED via update_status.
Attacker supplies IFC fragment with same element id to import_from_ifc → element replaced, status=PLANNED.
Or connect to TwinSynchronizer WS and send {type:'status_update', element_id:'WALL-001', status:'completed'} with no auth.
Or publish MQTT sensors/# spoofed values into bound structural properties.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior hunt discarded 'digital-twin WS' as near-miss without filing. This files the IFC silent overwrite (status wipe) as the primary SoR integrity chain, with WS/MQTT as the unauthenticated write amplifiers.
key_snippets: self.elements[element.element_id] = element  # import_from_ifc, no merge
status: ElementStatus = ElementStatus.PLANNED
elif msg_type == 'status_update': ... self.twin.update_status(...)
mqtt_client.subscribe("sensors/#")
PoC: COMPLETED → re-import → PLANNED

findings.title: site-logistics allocate_storage never persists usage → repeated calls overbook storage capacity
findings.description: allocate_storage copies zone.current_usage into a local zone_usage dict and increments only that local map. Successful allocations never write back to SiteZone.current_usage. A second call therefore starts from usage=0 again. Within one call, capacity is enforced (score -inf), but across calls a 100-ton yard accepts 90+90. get_storage_utilization also reads stale current_usage and reports available capacity that is already allocated.
findings.impact: Site logistics plans over-allocate physical storage → blocked unload bays, unsafe stockpile loading, and false JIT delivery readiness.
attack_path: Configure STORAGE zone capacity=100, current_usage=0.
allocate_storage([{id:M1, quantity:90, ...}]) → YARD.
allocate_storage([{id:M2, quantity:90, ...}]) → YARD again (persisted usage still 0).
get_storage_utilization still shows used=0 / available=100.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior 'site-logistics soft storage' discard referred to restriction soft-penalty (-100). This is hard capacity non-persistence across allocate_storage calls — distinct overbook root cause. Not resource-pool max-vs-sum.
key_snippets: zone_usage = {zid: zone.current_usage for zid, zone in storage_zones.items()}
zone_usage[best_zone] += material['quantity']  # never assigned back to zone.current_usage
if remaining_capacity < material['quantity']: return -float('inf')  # only within one call
PoC: 90+90 into capacity 100 across two calls
